subject: Content moderation at scale
text:
Hi [NAME],

We just onboarded an ads integrity team, helping them scale
auto-classification across markets. The main challenge was assembling
models, labelling and human QA together, to account for regional policy
variation and contextually-dependent content cues.

Here's how we're approaching it at Encord: we've built out a platform to
orchestrate model configuration (prompt + LLM pairing), model performance
evaluation and human labelling and verification in one place.

Would you be open to exchange perspectives on you're navigating this?

subject: the harder problem after quality
text:
Hi [NAME] ,

Congrats on the cinematic outputs from Seedance 2.0!

Generation quality is table stakes now. The harder problem we've seen is that aesthetics and contextual cues that resonate with one user segment can be completely different from another (ads creator vs. filmmaker; European vs. Chinese markets, etc.)

We help video generation teams like Synthesia, Flawless and Tavus navigate this - improving diversity of human feedback and automating annotation, evaluation and QA review workflows. The objective is richer fine-tuning data: time-aligned audio-visual datasets for SFT and multi-dimensional preference signals for RLHF.

How are you thinking about output alignment at [COMPANY]? Worth a quick chat?

subject: GenAI eval
text:
Hi [NAME], 

      Saw your work spanning booking, post-booking, and servicing - I imagine that means juggling multiple GenAI + predictive workflows, each with very different data quality and failure modes. 

      One common challenge we see across F500 and digital-native teams: GenAI performance ultimately depends on structured human feedback for evaluation. 

      That's where Encord fits - supporting preference ranking, pairwise comparisons, rubric-based eval across modalities, and curating eval sets around real failure modes. 

      Curious if this resonates on your side? Happy to compare notes in a quick 20-min intro chat.

subject: Engie & Encord | Post-Paris Invest Region Intro
text:
Bonjour [NAME],

J'ai eu la chance d'échanger avec votre collègue Sébastien lors de
l'événement Invest Paris Region la semaine dernière - il m'a suggéré de
vous contacter directement.

Si j'ai bien compris, vous travaillez sur la stratégie data transverse chez
Engie, en support d'un grand nombre de business units - c'est exactement le
type de périmètre où ce que nous construisons tend à être pertinent.
Lorsque les grands groupes énergétiques font monter en puissance leurs
programmes IA - gestion de réseau, inspection d'actifs, maintenance
prédictive - la couche données (curation, annotation, contrôle qualité à
l'échelle) devient un point de friction commun à toutes ces BUs.

Nous sommes la couche d'infrastructure data pour les équipes AI, et nous
travaillons avec des organisations qui opèrent à des niveaux similaires de
complexité et de volume de données multimodales.

Je me permets de joindre le deck présenté lors de l'événement - n'hésitez
pas à le partager en interne si vous pensez que cela peut intéresser les
bonnes équipes.

Ce serait vraiment intéressant d'échanger sur ce que vous observez en
interne et de voir si une collaboration a du sens. Je suis disponible pour
un court appel virtuel dans les prochaines semaines si vous le souhaitez.
Je vous laisse mon calendrier
<[LINK]>
si
c'est plus simple.

Bien cordialement,

Oil rigs in real time.

way and would love to compare notes with you

Would you be open to a quick call later this week? Love to compare notes

subject: Encord + 3D scan data - relevant to [COMPANY]'s ML pipeline?
text:
Hi [NAME],

I came across [COMPANY]'s work on FitTech; impressive what you've built
with 3D foot scanning, especially getting mobile reconstruction accurate
enough to drive fit recommendations at scale.

I'm reaching out [SENDER]. We work with ML teams building on 3D and
multimodal sensor data, and a few things we've shipped recently seem
directly relevant to what your team is likely dealing with:

   - *3D/point cloud annotation* - cuboid labeling, segmentation, and
   sensor fusion for depth + RGB data (overview here
   <[LINK]>
   )
   - *Keypoint & pose annotation* - skeleton-based landmark labeling for
   training measurement extraction models (guide
   <[LINK]>
   )
   - *Data curation at scale* - automatically surfacing low-quality or
   redundant training samples, which matters a lot when you're ingesting scan
   data across thousands of retail locations (Standard AI case study
   <[LINK]>
   )

Happy to show you how other CV teams are using Encord to tighten up their
data pipelines. Would a 20-minute call be worth it?
